ground_truth.description: The class's stated contract was that the MCP tool 'get_scheduler_state' serves a 1500-task snapshot under 50ms, but the test now times only the sync helper 'read_scheduler_state', bypassing the asyncio.to_thread handoff and FastMCP dispatch entirely. A regression in the actual MCP request path that blows the 50ms orchestrator budget would no longer be caught by this canary, so perf coverage of the promised end-to-end path is lost.

The change removes asyncio/FastMCP overhead but keeps an absolute wall-clock 50ms bound measured with time.perf_counter, which still includes OS scheduling latency. Under pytest-xdist -n auto with 32 workers on a contended CPU, the process can be descheduled for tens of milliseconds during json.loads of the ~500KB file, so the median-of-20 assertion can still intermittently trip — the de-flake root cause (CI load sensitivity of a wall-clock latency bound) is only partially addressed.

provenance.runs_db_query: SELECT task_id, project_id, outcome, review_cycles, verify_attempts FROM task_results WHERE review_cycles >= 1, cross-referenced with events (escalation_created, merge_finalized) -- see mining.mine_fn_candidates.
